Catering guide · 2026 Buffet, delivered or plated catering?

By the Messify team · Updated October 2026 · 4 min read

Quick answer

Delivered catering is the simplest and usually lowest-cost option, best for office lunches and small groups. A buffet setup suits parties, corporate events and weddings and handles large numbers well. Served or plated meals are the most formal and need the most staff. Family style and live stations sit in between.

The main catering styles

The service style shapes your budget, the space you need and how the event feels. Here is how the main options compare.

Catering styles compared
StyleStaff neededBest forWatch out for
Delivered, ready to serveLowestOffice lunches, meetings, small partiesYou or your team set out and serve the food
Buffet setupMediumParties, corporate events, weddingsNeeds space for a table and a queue
Served or platedHighestFormal dinners, award nights, VIP eventsNeeds the most staff and a fixed seating plan
Family style (shared platters)MediumFamily gatherings, team dinnersNeeds space on each table for platters
Live stationsMedium to highWeddings, receptions, larger partiesNeeds chefs on site, space and often power or gas

Delivered catering

The food arrives ready to serve, in trays or containers, and you set it out. It is the simplest and usually the lowest-cost option, and it suits office lunches, meetings and small gatherings where someone on your side can manage the table.

Buffet setup

The caterer sets up a full buffet at your venue, with dishes kept warm and the table arranged for guests to serve themselves. Buffets handle large numbers well, offer variety, and let guests choose what and how much they eat. Plan enough space for a queue: for more than about 60 guests, a table guests can reach from both sides keeps it moving.

Served or plated

Each guest is served at their seat, course by course. It is the most formal option and gives you full control over timing, but it needs the most staff, a fixed headcount and a seating plan, and it usually costs the most per person.

Family style

Shared platters go on each table and guests pass them around. It feels generous and social, and suits family gatherings and team dinners, but each table needs room for the platters.

Live stations

A chef cooks or carves in front of guests: grills, shawarma, pasta or desserts. Stations add a sense of occasion to weddings and receptions, but they need space, time and often power or gas at the venue, so check the venue rules first.

Which style suits your event?

  • Team lunch or meeting: delivered, or a simple buffet setup for bigger groups.
  • Birthday or family gathering at home: a buffet setup, or family style for a sit-down meal.
  • Corporate event or launch: a buffet setup, with live stations if you want a centrepiece.
  • Wedding: usually a buffet, sometimes with live stations; plated for smaller, formal weddings.
  • Formal dinner or awards night: served or plated.

Questions people ask

Is a buffet cheaper than a plated meal?

Usually, yes. A buffet needs fewer staff than serving each guest at their seat, so it tends to cost less per person for the same menu.

What is the difference between delivered catering and a buffet setup?

Delivered catering arrives ready to serve and you set it out. With a buffet setup, the caterer arranges the full buffet at your venue and keeps the food warm.

Which catering style is best for a large event?

A buffet handles large numbers well and offers variety. For several hundred guests, plan multiple serving points so queues stay short.

What are live stations?

Stations where a chef cooks or carves in front of guests, such as grills, shawarma, pasta or desserts. They need space, staff and often power or gas at the venue.
